QueueDepth.description:
How many jobs stand in each status.

`queued` and `running` are the work still to be done. The other three only grow.

RoleChange.description: What a user is to be allowed from now on.

Route.description: One courier's round trip from the depot through its stops.

distance_m.description: The length of the round trip in metres (D4).

distances.description:
What that length was measured along. Roads, where the solver has a routing
service to ask and was answered, and great circles otherwise (D66).

stops.description: In the order the courier calls.

RouteBudget.description:
How long the search for each route of a plan may go on (D31).

The limits are those of the search itself (D15): a span of time, a number of
candidate moves, or both, in which case whichever is reached first ends the search.
A value of this type has at least one of them, because annealing never ends on its
own (D18): [`RouteBudget::new`] and deserialization both check.

With moves alone, the same seed gives the same route (D5). A span of time cuts the
search wherever the machine has got to.

iterations.description:
Candidate moves for one route. With this limit alone, the same seed gives the
same route.

time_ms.description: Wall-clock time for one route, in milliseconds.

RouteId.description: One courier's route in a plan.

RouteJob.description:
A route job as someone watching its plan sees it: whose route it is, which stops it
has to put in order, and how the search for that order stands.

attempt.description: How many times the job has been claimed.

order_ids.description:
The courier's orders, as clustering left them. The `order` of a `RouteProgress`
counts into this list.

oneOf.description:
How far the search has got, as the last heartbeat stored it. That is a few
seconds old at most, and what is announced in between is fresher.
The worker of the latest claim.

RouteProgress.description:
How far the search for one route has got, as its worker announces it a few times a
second while it searches (D48, D49).

Nothing stores it. The next one replaces it, and one that is lost is not missed.

attempt.description:
Which claim of the job this comes from (D22). A worker that has lost the job may
go on announcing until its next heartbeat tells it so. What it says then has a
lower number than the job has.

best_cost_m.description: The length of the best route so far, in metres.

order.description:
The best route so far: its stops in calling order, each as its position in the
`order_ids` of the job. Left out when it would not fit a notification.

RouteStop.description: One call on a route, with what a map needs to draw it.

token.description: Sent with every later request, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Turns a day's parcel orders into courier routes.

To try it here: `POST /api/auth/login`, copy the `token` of the answer, press **Authorize** and paste it.

The same API is behind the map at `/`.

post.description:
The Telegram bot is the one caller of this. It shows its key, as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`, says which Telegram user it is talking to, and is
given a token for that user's account. With that token it asks what the user asks
of it, so the bot can do no more than the user may (D9).

A Telegram user the API has not heard of gets an account here and now: a client's,
with no address and no password. An admin can make it an operator's.

The token is good for `expires_in` seconds, which is far less than a login's: the
bot asks for one whenever it needs one.

post.description:
Stores the plan and hands it to the solvers. They take the orders of the day that
are pending, give each active courier the ones that fit it, and search for the
order to call in. Read the plan again to see it go from `queued` to `routing` to
`done`.

A day has one plan in progress at a time. The `X-Request-Id` of this request is
kept on the plan's jobs, so the solvers' logs can be searched for it.

get.description:
An event stream (`text/event-stream`) that stays open, for showing a plan while
the solvers are at it. It opens with the plan as it is, and then sends what
changes:

- `plan`: the plan, as `GET /api/plans/{id}` gives it, whenever its status or its
  counts have changed. When `routes_done` has grown, one route more can be read
  from `/api/plans/{id}/routes`.
- `jobs`: the plan's route jobs, an array of `RouteJob`, whenever one of them was
  claimed, stored, retried or stopped.
- `progress`: a `RouteProgress`, a few times a second for each route that is being
  searched for. It says how far the search has got and which route is the best so
  far.

A line that starts with a colon is a comment, sent to keep the connection open.
The stream ends when the token it was opened with expires. Opened again, it starts
with the plan as it is then.

`EventSource` in a browser cannot send the token. The page reads the stream with
`fetch`.

get.description:
An event stream (`text/event-stream`) that stays open. It opens with a `stats`
event, which is what `GET /api/system/stats` gives, and sends another whenever that
has changed: at once when a job is queued, claimed or finished, and within a couple
of seconds when a worker has come or has fallen silent.

It also sends an `orders` event, an `OrdersChanged`, whenever an order was placed
or withdrawn. It names the day and no order: whoever shows that day reads its
orders again. Nothing makes up for one that was lost, so a reader also reads now
and then without being told.

A line that starts with a colon is a comment, sent to keep the connection open.
The stream ends when the token it was opened with expires.
